provenance.paper: Watkins, C. J. C. H., & Dayan, P. (1992). Q-learning.
provenance.citation: Watkins, C. J. C. H., & Dayan, P. (1992). Machine Learning, 8(3-4), 279-292.
provenance.locus: Theorem (p. 281): Q-learning converges to Q* with probability 1 under bounded rewards and repeated sampling; one-step lookup Q*(s,a) = r + γ max_a' Q*(s',a').
provenance.notes: Two-state task: 'go' moves s0 to the terminal goal with reward 1, so the Bellman optimality equation gives Q*(s0,go) = 1 + γ·0 = 1 exactly; 'stay' self-loops with reward 0, Q*(s0,stay) = 0 + γ·max Q*(s0,·) = 0.9·Q*(s0,go) = 0.9. The learned table must satisfy these closed-form values and the greedy policy must choose 'go'.

input.intent: learn the optimal policy for the two-state goal task

expected.notes: Closed-form Bellman fixed point; Watkins-Dayan convergence checked against exact Q*.
